## Highlights

- Native deployment provisioning now accepts the Better Auth 1.7 built-in password capability. Upgrading a host that already runs v0.5.87 or v0.5.88 completes the break-glass administrator reconciliation instead of stopping after the service containers become healthy ([#4939](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4939)).
- [Coding agents sign in to the MCP endpoint without an API key, unless an operator turns that off](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4926). A person connects Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another agent by signing in from it, chooses one organization and how much the agent may do there, and the agent then works as that person, never above their role. Codex is no longer refused with `invalid_scope`: the scopes it asks for beyond what an agent may hold are dropped instead. API keys keep working. The upgrade notes below say what this asks of an operator.
- [**Settings** › **API** › **Connected agents**](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4925) lists the coding agents a person connected to the organization: each with its app and where it comes from (the domain it proved, or **Unverified**), the access it was given, when it connected and when it last called. Owners and Admins switch between **Mine** and **Everyone** and can **Show disconnected**. **Disconnect** asks first, and the agent loses access at once. While sign-in is on, the page appears for everyone who may connect an agent, and it always appears for a member who still holds a connection ([Connected agents](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/connected-agents)).
- [The automations list says whether each automation starts on its own](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4924). A **Trigger** column beside the status shows **Enabled**, **Paused** (it turned itself off after repeated failures), **Off** or **Not live** over the kind of trigger (**Schedule**, **Webhook** or **Platform event**), and **Manual** for an automation without one, so a schedule that paused itself no longer reads like one that runs ([Automations](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/catalog)).
- [A task's activity shows its agent runs in the timeline](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4683). **View** on a run shows its status, duration, tool actions, cost and log in place; consecutive runs fold into one row.

## Upgrade notes

- From v0.5.88 to v0.5.89 the backend applies one database migration at boot and the API contract moves from `3.43.0` to `3.44.0`; neither needs a manual step. Coding-agent sign-in turns on unless you turn it off, so decide about it before you upgrade; and an organization whose model-access rules lack a target cannot change its model access until it repairs them (both below). Rerun the normal Tale CLI deployment/adoption flow after the images and CLI are published.
- The migration, `0204_usage_ledger_provider.sql`, adds the table `app.usage_ledger_provider`, which inherits `app.usage_ledger`, and its two indexes, so that usage is booked per provider and **Top models** in usage analytics no longer merges one model ID that two providers serve ([#4241](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4241)). It changes no existing row: usage booked before the upgrade stays merged. The previous image is safe to keep serving while it applies, and books usage the old way until it retires.
- The API contract `3.44.0` adds the `agentOAuth` security scheme beside the API key on the MCP endpoint, and the sign-in discovery documents answer on a default deployment. No operation, schema or API key behaviour changes.
- Coding-agent sign-in is on by default from this release ([#4926](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4926)), although the v0.5.88 notes said it stays off unless an operator turns it on. `TALE_MCP_CLIENT_METADATA_DOCUMENTS` covers agents that publish a client metadata document, such as Claude Code and Codex, and `TALE_MCP_DYNAMIC_CLIENT_REGISTRATION` covers agents that register themselves, such as Cursor and VS Code. Both now count as `true` when unset, so a deployment that never set them turns sign-in on when it upgrades. That opens public surfaces: the `/.well-known/oauth-*` discovery documents, the sign-in server's `/api/auth/oauth2/*` endpoints with rate-limited self-registration, and the consent page at `/oauth/consent`. Tale's proxy routes the discovery documents, and a proxy of your own must forward `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource*` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server*` at the host root; Claude Code and Codex also need outbound HTTPS from the backend to their vendor's host (`claude.ai`, `chatgpt.com`). [Let coding agents sign in](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/authentication#coding-agent-sign-in) and [Harden a production deployment](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/operate/security/hardening#agent-sign-in) say what to check before leaving it on. To keep agents on API keys, set both to `false` and recreate the backend. If you turn it off later, the agents connected until then lose access at once. The [v0.5.90 notes](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/releases/tag/v0.5.90) repeat this for deployments that upgrade past v0.5.89.
- Two sandbox settings behave differently ([#4169](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4169)). An explicit `SANDBOX_MAX_SESSIONS` now also turns adaptive memory admission off: new sessions are no longer held back for host memory, so size it from measured peaks; the disk floor and the CPU-pressure check still apply. With `SANDBOX_MAX_SESSIONS` unset, a `SANDBOX_MIN_FREE_MEMORY` at or above the Docker host's total memory now stops the sandbox at boot with a configuration error, when the sandbox can read the host's memory at boot. Set it below the host's memory, or to `0` to remove the reserve ([Environment reference](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/environment-reference#sandbox-infrastructure)).
- Model-access rules for a user, team or role now need a target ([#4216](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4216)). A rule an earlier release saved without one still applies to no one, and **Settings** › **Governance** › **Models** now shows it as **Missing target**. Until each such rule has a target or is deleted there, no model-access change saves from that page, the **Model endpoints for API keys** switch included; the API and MCP refuse a `model_access` policy that keeps such a rule, and `tale config platform` cannot declare `model_access` while one is stored. Tale guesses no target and removes no rule on its own ([Models](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/content-models#restrict-model-access)).
- Saving **Settings** › **Enterprise SSO** no longer removes the claim mappings stored for an OIDC connection ([#4212](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4212)). On earlier releases any save, even of the display name alone, removed them, and this release does not bring back mappings already removed: if your identity provider needs them, check that they are still set.
- The native CLI still refuses a disabled or malformed password policy and verifies the declared credential hash before completing provisioning.
- These notes were corrected after v0.5.89 was published ([#4970](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4970)): they first said that no database migration or manual configuration change was needed and described only the native CLI fix.
